drivingQuestion: How long is the mishna's 'period required for tanning', and which halakhot are governed by the distance of four mil?
outcomeNote: The measure is fixed at four mil; the tradition is reattributed to Aivu and extended to four cases, and its scope is then limited to what lies ahead of the traveler.

segments.he: לֹא: טְלָאָהּ, הִילֵּךְ – אִין, לֹא הִילֵּךְ – לָא.
segments.en: The Gemara explains: «No,» this is not difficult. «Sewing» the ear is an action that nullifies the ear’s classification as flesh. But spreading skin on the ground is not an action that nullifies the skin’s classification as flesh unless one trod upon the skin. Therefore, if one «trod» upon the skin it «is» no longer classified as flesh, but if one «did not tread» upon it, it does «not» cease being classified as flesh.

segments.he: כַּמָּה כְּדֵי עִבּוּד? אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: אַרְבַּעַת מִילִין.
segments.en: The mishna states that the skin must be trodden upon for the period required for tanning. The Gemara clarifies: «How long is the period» required «for tanning? Rav Huna says» that «Rabbi Yannai says:» The time which it takes one to walk «four mil.»

segments.he: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִשּׁוּם דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לְגַבָּל.
segments.en: §Since the period of time it takes to walk four mil was mentioned, the Gemara lists halakhot that employ this period of time. «Rabbi Abbahu says in the name of Reish Lakish: With regard to» a professional «kneader» who is careful to maintain the ritual purity of the dough that he kneads for others, he must walk up to four mil in order to purify the vessel he is using by immersing it in a ritual bath. He is not required to walk farther than this unless the person hiring him pays for him to do so.

«And» similarly, «with regard to prayer,» one who is traveling may not pray where he is if there is a synagogue within four mil ahead of him, but rather must continue traveling in order to pray in the synagogue. «And» similarly, «with regard to washing» one’s «hands» before eating, one who is traveling may not eat without washing his hands if there is water within «four mil» ahead of him.
With regard to this statement of Reish Lakish, «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:»

segments.he: אַיְבוּ אַמְרַהּ, וְאַרְבְּעֵי אֲמַר בַּהּ, וַחֲדָא מִינַּיְיהוּ עֲבוֹדָה.
segments.en: It was «Aivu» who «said» this statement in the name of Reish Lakish and not Rabbi Abbahu, «and he said four» halakhot, not three, with regard to the measure of four mil, «and» the fourth «one of them» is the halakha mentioned in the mishna: Skins that one spread on the ground and trod upon for the period required for «tanning,» i.e., the amount of time it takes to walk four mil, are no longer classified as flesh and are ritually pure.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְפָנָיו, אֲבָל לְאַחֲרָיו – אֲפִילּוּ מִיל אֶחָד אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר. רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר, וּמִינַּהּ: מִיל הוּא דְּאֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר, הָא פָּחוֹת מִמִּיל – חוֹזֵר.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says:» With regard to prayer and washing one’s hands, the Sages «taught» that one must travel four mil to find a synagogue or water «only» if the synagogue or the water is «ahead of him,» in the direction that he is traveling. «But» if it is «behind him, he» need «not return even one mil. Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov said: From» this statement one may infer that «it is» specifically «a mil that one» need «not return; but one must return» for a synagogue or water that is at a distance of «less than» one «mil.»

moves.summary: answers the standing difficulty by distinguishing sewing an ear from spreading a hide, which loses its status as flesh only if trodden upon
moves.about: whether spreading a hide on the ground nullifies its status as flesh the way sewing an ear does — it does so only if one trod upon it

moves.summary: asks the measure of the mishna's phrase 'the period required for tanning'
moves.about: how long the period the mishna calls 'kedei ibbud', the time required for tanning, actually is

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא אמר רבי ינאי
moves.summary: answers in R' Yannai's name: the time it takes to walk four mil
moves.about: the measure of the mishna's 'period required for tanning' — the time it takes to walk four mil

moves.cueHe: רבי אבהו משום דריש לקיש אמר
moves.summary: appends, in Reish Lakish's name, that a professional kneader must go up to four mil to immerse his vessel
moves.about: the halakhot governed by the four-mil distance — a professional kneader, prayer, and washing the hands

moves.summary: continues the same list: prayer and washing the hands are likewise measured at four mil
corrects the tradition: Aivu said it, and in four cases, the fourth being the tanning of the mishna
moves.about: who transmitted Reish Lakish's four-mil rulings — Aivu, and in four cases rather than three

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: לא שנו אלא לפניו
moves.summary: limits the four-mil rule to what lies ahead of the traveler; behind him he need not return even a mil
moves.about: that the four-mil requirement for prayer and hand-washing was taught only where the synagogue or water lies ahead of the traveler, not behind him

moves.cueHe: רב אחא בר יעקב אמר, ומינה
moves.summary: infers from that wording that less than a mil one must in fact retrace
moves.about: reading R' Yosei b'R Ḥanina's 'not even one mil' precisely — a full mil one need not go back, but less than a mil one must
